abstract: We resolve Erd\H{o}s Problem~521 by proving that the normalized real-root count $N_n/\log n$ of Rademacher polynomials almost surely has no limit. More generally, consider the Kac polynomials \[ P_n(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\xi_jx^j \] with i.i.d.\ real coefficients of mean zero, variance one, and a finite absolute exponential moment. Let $N_n$ denote the number of distinct real roots of $P_n$. We prove that, almost surely, \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1\pi, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1\pi+C_*, \] and the set of subsequential limits is exactly \[ \left[\frac1\pi,\;\frac1\pi+C_*\right]. \] Here $C_*>1/\pi$ is a constant uniquely determined by an equation. The lower-limit identity remains valid under the weaker assumption that $\mathbb{E}|\xi_0|^{2+\delta}<\infty$ for some $\delta>0$.
hook: Real roots of random polynomials never settle to a steady growth rate, answering an Erdős question.
summary: For random polynomials with independent coefficients, the count of real roots divided by log n keeps oscillating forever between two constants, one of them 1/pi. This settles Erdős Problem 521 and generalizes it to many coefficient distributions. The upper constant is defined only implicitly by an equation.
title: the limit point set of real roots of random polynomials: a resolution of erd\H{o}s problem 521
